acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Given a feature's Requirements/Tech-Spec, approved at Gate 1, when the WBS generation step runs, then a phase-enumeration call decides ONLY the ordered phase list (`id`/`type`/`title`/`sourceUC`/`commit`), never any task
Given the phase list from AC-01, when the WBS generation step continues, then one bounded call per phase, in the SAME order enumerated, produces that phase's own tasks only

Given a phase's own task-generation call, when dispatched, then it receives that phase's own Requirements detail, the Tech-Spec skeleton (with `needsComponentDetail` available), and every PRIOR phase's own task id/title/outcome/domain — never a later phase's tasks

Given phase N's own task-generation call succeeds, when the next phase (N+1) has not yet been generated, then phase N's tasks are persisted to `index.json` immediately — a later failure/crash does not lose them

Given a resumed run where phases 1..K already have `index.json` entries and phase K+1 does not, when WBS generation re-runs, then generation resumes from phase K+1 — phases 1..K are never redispatched

Given a complete, multi-phase skeleton produced via this feature's own per-phase flow, when `wb-skeleton-check.js`/`wb-graph-checks.js`/`wb-validate.js` run against it, then all pass exactly as they do today

Given the complete skeleton from AC-06, when `gaia-generate-work-breakdown-task` (the existing per-task DETAIL pass) runs, then it is unaffected — reads the fully-assembled skeleton exactly as it does today

Given a per-phase call reports `needsComponentDetail`, when the host processes its response, then the SAME bounded, single-round drill-down FTR-032 already built fires, scoped to that one phase's call
Given all changes are delivered, when `npm test` runs, then all tests pass: new regression/integration tests for AC-01 through AC-08, and a full-suite regression
